coach_lessons.trigger_question: Which has more sides, a trapezoid or a square?
coach_lessons.initial_wrong_answer: trapezoid (used >= so tied 4 vs 4 picked the first item)
coach_lessons.self_analysis_question: Why did my comparison rule fail when two shapes have the exact same number of straight sides (4 vs 4)?
coach_lessons.conceptual_hypothesis: In arithmetic and English, 'A has more than B' means strict inequality (sides(A) > sides(B)). When sides(A) == sides(B), A is NOT more than B, so the strict condition (4 > 4) is false. Verified on 8 tie-case examples in K/mathematics/shape-sides.train.jsonl.

coach_lessons.trigger_question: What shape/colour is the largest object when shapes are rotated by an arbitrary angle theta in [0, pi]?
coach_lessons.initial_wrong_answer: Confused rotated squares/diamonds/pentagons and mis-ranked rectangle vs diamond radius
coach_lessons.expected_answer: Rotation-invariant 2D covariance eigenvalues, dimensionless compactness (Area / R_max^2), and radial harmonics (|F3|, |F4|, |F5|)
coach_lessons.self_analysis_question: Why did axis-aligned bounding-box aspect ratio and fill fraction change when the exact same shape was tilted?
coach_lessons.conceptual_hypothesis: Physical shape identity is invariant under 2D rigid rotation SO(2). By replacing axis-aligned bounding boxes with principal eigenvalue elongation E = sqrt(lambda_max / lambda_min), dimensionless compactness gamma = Area / R_max^2, principal kurtosis, and shape-specific generative radius r = sqrt(Area / c_shape), visual recognition becomes invariant to rotation.

coach_lessons.trigger_question: Fill the blank: ____ is a word at the start or end of a sentence or after 'Mr.' abbreviation
coach_lessons.initial_wrong_answer: Lost left/right context when splitting sentences hard on '.' and using only 2-word trigrams
coach_lessons.expected_answer: Continuous sliding-window stream with 3-word left/right and wide-surround dendritic contexts
coach_lessons.self_analysis_question: Why did 5 out of 120 McGuffey Reader cloze items fail when the missing word sat near punctuation or common bigrams?
coach_lessons.conceptual_hypothesis: Human cortical reading maintains continuous temporal context across punctuation and integrates 3-step distal dendritic associations (w_{-3}, w_{-2}, w_{-1}, w_{+1}, w_{+2}, w_{+3}). Indexing the continuous word stream with 3-gram and wide-surround links resolves ambiguity.
